title: Substitution and numerical value of algebraic expressions

steps.title: Move the value into the slot
steps.action: Put three where the x appears.
steps.narration: The variable is a place for a given number.

steps.title: Calculate the output
steps.action: Three plus four equals seven.
steps.narration: The expression has numerical value seven.

worked_examples.misconception: Keeping x in the calculation after substitution.
worked_examples.repair: Point to x, cover it and replace it with 3.

worked_examples.skill: Keep a signed input in brackets

model.description: Keep a signed input in brackets

steps.title: Place negative two in the a slot
steps.action: Write 3(-2), keeping the minus inside brackets.
steps.narration: Juxtaposition means multiplication, not addition.

steps.title: Multiply with signs
steps.action: Positive three times negative two is negative six.
steps.narration: The negative input stays attached to its value.

worked_examples.misconception: Reading 3a as 3+a or dropping the negative.
worked_examples.repair: Show the multiplication dot and the signed chip.

steps.title: Put the full signed value in the base
steps.action: Use (-3)², not -3².
steps.narration: Brackets tell the square to act on the negative value.

steps.title: Open the square
steps.action: Write two factors of negative three.
steps.narration: The exponent two makes two complete copies.

steps.title: Multiply both negatives
steps.action: Negative three times negative three is positive nine.
steps.narration: An even number of negative factors is positive.

worked_examples.misconception: Squaring three but leaving a minus outside.
worked_examples.repair: Circle the base and duplicate its brackets.

worked_examples.skill: Distinguish a negative outside the square

model.description: Distinguish a negative outside the square

steps.title: Mark the base of each power
steps.action: For -x² the minus is outside x²; for (-x)² it is inside.
steps.narration: Exponent scope controls the sign.

steps.title: Square the two bases
steps.action: Negative two squared is four; negative of negative two is positive two.
steps.narration: The outside minus has not been squared.

steps.title: Complete both branches
steps.action: Take negative four in the first branch and positive four in the second.
steps.narration: The two numerical values differ.

worked_examples.repair: Put a bracket boundary around each base first.

steps.title: Substitute with brackets
steps.action: Put negative four into the x slot while retaining plus five.
steps.narration: The coefficient two multiplies the input first.

steps.title: Multiply before adding
steps.action: Two times negative four is negative eight.
steps.narration: The addition remains visible for the next action.

steps.title: Add the constant
steps.action: Negative eight plus five is negative three.
steps.narration: Follow the order of operations.

worked_examples.misconception: Adding five to negative four before multiplying.
worked_examples.repair: Point to multiplication first, then addition.

steps.title: Fill both named slots
steps.action: Put two for a and negative one for b; do not swap them.
steps.narration: Each variable has its own colour and value.

steps.title: Multiply each term
steps.action: Four times two is eight; three times negative one is negative three.
steps.narration: Keep subtraction of the negative product visible.

steps.title: Resolve double negative
steps.action: Eight minus negative three equals eleven.
steps.narration: Subtracting a negative adds three.

worked_examples.misconception: Replacing both a and b with the same number.
worked_examples.repair: Use separate value chips for a and b.

steps.title: Replace only x inside the bracket
steps.action: Write negative two in its own brackets; leave the outer two outside.
steps.narration: The outside two multiplies the whole difference.

steps.title: Calculate inside first
steps.action: Negative two minus three is negative five.
steps.narration: Close the inside operation before multiplying.

steps.title: Multiply the group
steps.action: Two times negative five is negative ten.
steps.narration: The whole group is one signed factor.

worked_examples.misconception: Distributing two to x but not the constant, or skipping the inner subtraction.
worked_examples.repair: Keep a border around the bracket until its value is known.

steps.title: Substitute into both x slots
steps.action: Put (-3) in the square and in the linear term.
steps.narration: One given value fills every occurrence of x.

steps.title: Do powers and products
steps.action: Negative three squared is nine; two times negative three is negative six.
steps.narration: Subtract the entire negative product.

steps.title: Finish the signed subtraction
steps.action: Nine minus negative six is fifteen.
steps.narration: The result is positive fifteen.

worked_examples.repair: Show both occurrences and settle powers and products first.

worked_examples.skill: Evaluate a fraction and a constant

model.description: Evaluate a fraction and a constant

steps.title: Place the input in the numerator
steps.action: Write negative four over two, keeping plus three outside the fraction bar.
steps.narration: Only x is divided by two.

steps.title: Divide before adding
steps.action: Negative four divided by two is negative two.
steps.narration: The outside three is unchanged.

steps.title: Add at the end
steps.action: Negative two plus three is one.
steps.narration: The fraction bar has a limited scope.

worked_examples.misconception: Dividing x+3 by two instead of only x.
worked_examples.repair: Draw the fraction bar boundary before substituting.

worked_examples.q: Evaluate 5/(x-1) at x=3 and at x=1.
worked_examples.answer: At x=3 the value is 5/2; at x=1 it is undefined.

steps.title: Substitute separately
steps.action: Use a distinct denominator lane for three and for one.
steps.narration: The denominator is the complete x minus one group.

steps.title: Calculate denominators
steps.action: Three minus one is two; one minus one is zero.
steps.narration: A zero denominator signals an invalid input.

steps.title: Report both outcomes
steps.action: Five over two is valid; five over zero is undefined.
steps.narration: Do not cancel or invent a value for the invalid branch.

worked_examples.misconception: Treating 5/0 as zero or allowing x=1.
worked_examples.repair: Calculate the whole denominator before dividing.

worked_examples.skill: Evaluate a three-term expression with two inputs

model.description: Evaluate a three-term expression with two inputs

steps.title: Fill every named occurrence
steps.action: Replace both a slots with negative two and both b slots with three.
steps.narration: Retain a bracket around each signed input.

steps.title: Calculate powers and inner product
steps.action: Negative two squared is four; negative two times three is negative six; three squared is nine.
steps.narration: Do these multiplications before adding terms.

steps.title: Resolve the signed middle term
steps.action: Negative three times negative six is positive eighteen.
steps.narration: The middle result increases the total.

steps.title: Add the three values
steps.action: Eight plus eighteen plus nine is thirty five.
steps.narration: All three original terms have contributed.

worked_examples.misconception: Dropping the sign of a in one of its occurrences.
worked_examples.repair: Colour every a slot the same before inserting (-2).

steps.title: Fill both pathways
steps.action: Put negative two in each complete expression.
steps.narration: Equivalent forms should give the same result at the same input.

steps.title: Evaluate inside each path
steps.action: First bracket gives two; second expression gives negative six plus twelve.
steps.narration: Keep two independent calculations visible.

steps.title: Compare numerical outputs
steps.action: Both paths end at six.
steps.narration: This input confirms agreement here; a single test alone is not proof for all x.

worked_examples.verify: At x=-2, 3(2)=6 and -6+12=6; distribution also shows 3(x+4)=3x+12 for all x.
worked_examples.misconception: Claiming equal outputs at one input proves equivalence generally.
worked_examples.repair: Verify this input, then show the distribution identity.

worked_examples.q: A learner evaluates 2x² at x=-3 as -18. Find the first error and correct it.
worked_examples.answer: They used -3² instead of (-3)²; the value is 18.

steps.title: Find the substitution slot
steps.action: The learner wrote a minus without grouping the value negative three.
steps.narration: The exponent applies to the whole substituted value.

steps.title: Show the first correct mathematical action
steps.action: Write two times negative three in parentheses squared.
steps.narration: The two negative factors make positive nine.

steps.title: Repair the calculation
steps.action: Two times nine is eighteen.
steps.narration: The learner claim negative eighteen fails the original expression.

worked_examples.repair: Draw the exponent scope around both parentheses.

worked_examples.q: A rectangle has length 4 cm and width (x+1) cm. Its perimeter is P=2(l+w). Find P when x=3.

steps.title: Calculate the width first
steps.action: Substitute three in x plus one to get four centimetres.
steps.narration: The width depends on x; length is already known.

steps.title: Put both dimensions into perimeter
steps.action: Two groups of length plus width gives two times eight.
steps.narration: Every side is counted: four, four, four and four.

steps.title: Multiply and keep the unit
steps.action: Two times eight is sixteen centimetres.
steps.narration: Perimeter uses a length unit, not square centimetres.

worked_examples.misconception: Using area units or only one pair of sides.
worked_examples.repair: Trace all four boundary sides on the rectangle.

worked_examples.skill: Evaluate with mixed operations and a denominator

model.description: Evaluate with mixed operations and a denominator

steps.title: Insert the signed input everywhere
steps.action: All three x positions receive negative two with brackets.
steps.narration: The denominator is nonzero at negative two.

steps.title: Resolve powers, brackets and quotient
steps.action: The square is four, inner bracket negative six, six over negative two is negative three.
steps.narration: Respect the boundaries of each operation.

steps.title: Multiply the remaining factors
steps.action: Three times four is twelve; negative two times negative six is positive twelve.
steps.narration: Keep the negative three fraction result visible.

steps.title: Add the three terms
steps.action: Twelve plus twelve minus three is twenty one.
steps.narration: Each branch contributes once to the total.

worked_examples.misconception: Cancelling the negative denominator or dropping the bracket sign.
worked_examples.repair: Build three parallel calculation lanes before combining.

practice_questions: Evaluate a²-2ab+b² when a=-1 and b=2.
Correct a learner who reports x²=-16 when x=-4.
Bracket the negative four before squaring.
A rectangle has length 5 cm and width x+2 cm. Find P=2(l+w) at x=1.
Calculate width, then trace four sides.
mastery_questions: A rectangle has length x+2 cm and width 2x-1 cm. Find P=2(l+w) at x=3 and verify four sides.
At x=3, l=5 and w=5; P=2(5+5)=20 cm; four sides total 5+5+5+5=20 cm.
